question: A project lead has let a project's knowledge base grow to hundreds of documents, including several superseded versions of the same policy. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) Retrieval will stop working altogether once the knowledge base grows past the model's context window.
B) Retrieval will hold the project to the plan's smallest context window until documents have been removed.
C) Retrieval may surface an outdated version, giving confident answers that no amount of reprompting fixes.
D) Retrieval will require her to configure a search index before the project can answer any questions.
correct_answers: C) Retrieval may surface an outdated version, giving confident answers that no amount of reprompting fixes.
explanations: Incorrect. It is precisely at that point that retrieval activates automatically, holding far more content than a window alone.
Incorrect. The window is determined by the model in use; retrieval extends reach over the knowledge base rather than shrinking it.
Correct. When the wrong source is retrieved, the answer is wrong at the root. Rewording the prompt cannot correct a problem that lives in the knowledge base itself.
Incorrect. No setup or configuration is required; retrieval turns itself on when the knowledge base grows large enough.
